Foreign key constraints, indexes, composite unique keys

findings.title: Spiders table defines unique constraint on ['slug'] instead of composite ['domain', 'slug']
findings.description: In database/migrations/2026_01_01_000000_create_scraper_tables.php, the spiders table creates a unique index on ['slug']. While default domain architecture uses isolated per-domain databases, if multiple domains share a single database, two spiders with the same slug across different domains will collide.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether spider slugs should be unique globally or per domain (unique(['domain', 'slug'])).
findings.decision_context:
Option A (Recommended): Keep unique(['domain', 'slug']) to allow identical spider slugs across different business domains when sharing a database.
Option B: Keep unique(['slug']) requiring globally unique spider slugs across all domains.

findings.title: Missing explicit index on raw_content_missing_periods.raw_content_id for high-volume analytics queries
findings.description: Foreign keys are constrained with cascade delete, but explicit composite indexes for raw_content_missing_periods range queries (raw_content_id, missing_since_at) enhance PostgreSQL/MySQL query performance.
findings.evidence: Schema::create('raw_content_missing_periods', ...) defines foreignId without explicit index() on composite missing queries.
findings.recommendation: Add index on ['raw_content_id', 'missing_since_at'] for optimized historical queries.
